transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Mendez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (ZenWave), Liam O'Connor (ZenWave SRE), Mei Tan (ZenWave DS)

---
[00:00] Carlos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you making time. We got Priya from our solutions team, she'll run through the embeddings and rerank flow. Quick check, is 42 minutes still ok?
[00:18] Aisha: Yep works for us, thanks.
[00:22] Priya: Cool, hi all. I'll, I'll share my screen in a sec. The plan: quick intro, then a live walkthrough of hosted embeddings + rerank, show how you can plug into your search pipeline, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:36] Liam: Sounds good. We're mostly interested in improving our onsite search relevance — current stack is Elastic with some TF-IDF and a small neural reranker. Latency budget is 200ms p95 for web search.
[00:50] Priya: Great note. We'll show both a low-latency candidate generation approach and a more accurate rerank that trades a bit of cost for quality.
[01:05] Priya: Ok, opening the Redwood Console — apologies if the org name shows as "Redwood-Dev" on my side — interface shows the hosted endpoints: /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank. You can call embeddings with a payload, get back a vector, default dims depend on model; in this demo we're using the redwood-embed-large (vector dim 1,024) — oh, you might see it listed as "rwood-embed-large" in the UI, the auto transcriptions sometimes, uh, older naming.
[01:40] Aisha: Is 1024 the default? We currently use 768 with our models. Wondering about storage and cost.
[01:48] Priya: Great question. We support multiple embedding model configs — 768, 1024 and a smaller 384. For search, 768 is often good; 1024 gives marginal improvements at higher storage/cost. Example: indexing 100k docs at 768 is roughly X GB, at 1024 it's ~1.33x. We'll include exact numbers in the benchmark sheet.
[02:15] Carlos: Also want to highlight batching — hosted API supports client-side batching and we do server-side optimizations. If you batch to 32 items you can vastly reduce per-item cost; though for online query embedding it's usually single-shot.
[02:33] Mei: For our use case we embed at index time and do realtime for query, yes. How about similarity search — do you recommend vector DBs or we can just store embeddings in our DB?
[02:46] Priya: Both options are common. For small scale you can store vectors in Postgres with pgvector, but for 100k+ we recommend a vector index (FAISS/Annoy) — Redwood focuses on the inference piece, we plug into whatever nearest-neighbor store you prefer. In the rerank pattern we demonstrated today, candidate gen is via your ANN index then we call /v1/rerank to reorder top K.
[03:08] Aisha: Show the rerank call?
[03:12] Priya: Sure. Example cURL: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"query": "how to reset password", "candidates": [ {"id":"doc1","text":"Resetting your password..."}, {"id":"doc2","text":"Password change guide..."} ] }' and you get back a scored list with normalized scores.
[03:45] Liam: What happens under the hood — is rerank using embeddings or cross-encoder?
[03:51] Priya: Good flag. Our rerank endpoint supports two modes: embedding-based dot-product rescoring (cheap, fast) and a cross-attention model (higher accuracy, higher latency). In hosted we set reasonable timeouts; cross-attention typically adds 50–150ms per item depending on model size.
[04:12] Aisha: That could push us above p95. Any mitigations?
[04:16] Priya: Yes — common pattern: do ANN retrieval to get top 100 candidates, then run a cheap embedding similarity to trim to top 10, finally run cross-encoder rerank only on those 10. That keeps p95 manageable while improving relevance. Also Redwood Optimize can suggest batching, caching prefixes, and quantization options for lower cost.
[04:48] Carlos: Also note dedicated pools if you need consistent tail latency — sometimes customers pick dedicated GPU capacity for predictable p95. But for many SaaS customers, hosted is fine with fallback models.
[05:03] Mei: On that note, data residency: we need logs/audit and data separation. Can hosted meet our compliance?
[05:12] Carlos: We do SOC2 currently; for stricter controls we offer Private (VPC/on-prem) with KMS integrations. Our hosted plane can redact and not persist request bodies when configured, and we support customer-managed keys for encryption at rest.
[05:32] Aisha: When you say KMS, do you mean AWS KMS only? We have GCP KMS.
[05:37] Priya: We integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS, yes. There's also an HSM option for Private environments. Side note: sometimes the UI shows "K M S" as three letters or the transcriber writes it funny as "KMSA" but it's the same.
[05:53] Liam: Ok thanks. On quotas, what's the rate limit? If we run a POC, do you throttle?
[05:59] Carlos: We have per-account quotas, but for POCs we typically bump the rate and provide temporary tokens; we'll coordinate that in the POC kickoff.
[06:12] Priya: Back to rerank scoring — we'll show an example where the embedding-based rerank fails on negation and the cross-encoder corrects it. 
[06:26] [screen share switches to demo dataset: 10 sample docs]
[06:30] Priya: Query: "how to cancel subscription" — embedding sim returns docs that mention "billing" and some about "upgrade", our cross-encoder picks the one that explicitly has cancellation steps. 
[06:45] Mei: Nice. Can you share the scoring outputs?
[06:48] Priya: Yep — here's the JSON: candidate list with scores. You'll see cross-attention scores are more tightly separated / more confident. There's also an explain endpoint (we have a small LIME-like output) but it's experimental.
[07:05] Aisha: You mentioned cost per 1k tokens for cross-encoder?
[07:10] Carlos: Typical numbers we'll provide in the sheet — rough rule: embedding calls are cheapest, rerank cross-encoder is 10–50x more depending on sequence length. But because rerank runs only on top K it's still economical.
[07:28] Liam: How about latency when batch reranking 10 docs? Does that scale linearly?
[07:33] Priya: There is some parallelism; on our hosted endpoints we do concurrent batching across the calls, but per-request latency can grow with K. We recommend trimming to top 10–20. Also we do KV cache for model context; sometimes the transcriber will say "K-V cash" but it's KV cache. That helps for chat-style contexts, less for rerank.
[07:55] Aisha: Any code examples for integrating with our existing elastic pipeline?
[07:59] Priya: Yes — we have a playbook: 1) index docs and store embeddings in FAISS; 2) on query, get ANN top 100; 3) embed query and do dot-product to reduce to top 20; 4) call rerank cross-encoder for top 10; 5) return results. I'll send the repo link after.
[08:20] Mei: Great. For the POC, we want to run on ~100k docs and measure MAP@10 and p95 latency. Is that feasible?
[08:27] Carlos: Absolutely, that's a standard POC. We'll help with benchmark configs.
[08:32] [09:00] Aisha: There's also a question of locking to a single model vs model switching. Can hosted do A/B or can we pin models?
[09:08] Priya: You can pin versions and do canary rollouts via the Console; Redwood Console supports route-level rollouts and fallback policies. For hosted, we offer model variants and automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity is constrained.
[09:25] Liam: Any mention of vendor lock-in? We don't want to be stuck with proprietary formats.
[09:30] Carlos: We try to be open — embeddings are standard vectors, and you can export artifacts; we also publish model profiles and you can run on private if you prefer. Competitors like Algolia/Elastic have different tradeoffs — Algolia is great for speed but less ML-first rerank.
[09:50] Mei: Ok, show me the Console metrics for token-level cost and latency.
[09:55] Priya: Sure — switching to the Console metrics page. Here you'll see per-route token breakdown, p95 latency, and model-level cost. There's an optimization tab that suggests batch sizes and a quantization profile (INT8) for dedupe / offline workloads.
[10:22] Aisha: For compliance, do you provide audit logs per request?
[10:26] Carlos: Yes — request-level audit logs with RBAC, and we retain logs per your retention policy. For hosted we can export logs to your SIEM.
[10:36] Liam: If we export logs, any PII concerns?
[10:39] Priya: We support on-the-fly redaction rules and you can opt out of storing raw request bodies.
[10:48] Aisha: Great. Back to relevance: do you have automated eval hooks? We saw mention of Redwood Optimize.
[10:55] Carlos: Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals against a seed prompt set, track regressions, and suggest model/quantization/batching changes. For the POC we can enable an eval suite to measure MAP, MRR, etc.
[11:10] Mei: Will you send the eval template?
[11:12] Priya: Yes, included in the post-call package.
[11:16] [11:30] Aisha: Question from product: what's the SLA for hosted?
[11:34] Carlos: Hosted has best-effort with a published uptime target; Dedicated gets SLA credits. For production-critical search we often recommend Dedicated or private for strict SLAs. But many customers start hosted and migrate.
[11:50] Liam: If we start with hosted, can we later migrate our keys and data to Private?
[11:56] Priya: Yes — migration paths are supported. We also support region pinning to meet residency needs.
[12:06] Aisha: Anything about cost savings for batching at index time?
[12:09] Carlos: Index-time batching is the biggest saver; you can also apply quantization to embeddings to cut storage. We'll include concrete cost examples in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[12:22] Mei: What about scaling — do you autoscale?
[12:24] Priya: Hosted autoscaling is automatic; Dedicated gives you reserved pools with autoscale policies and burst options.
[12:34] [13:00] Aisha: Okay I want to call out a couple constraints: enterprise procurement needs SOC2, SAML/SSO, and confirmation we can do GCP KMS. Also SRE wants to run end-to-end latency tests.
[13:16] Carlos: Noted — we'll include SOC2 and SAML docs. We'll also provide ephemeral test tokens for the SRE team to run load tests.
[13:28] Liam: We'll need some sample curl commands and a small script to pump queries.
[13:33] Priya: I'll attach sample scripts.
[13:36] Aisha: Competitors: we've spoken to Algolia and Elastic; Algolia's speed is appealing but they lack the ML-first rerank. Elastic gives more control but more ops overhead.
[13:50] Carlos: Totally — Redwood sits between: managed hosted inference plus ML-first rerank.
[13:58] Mei: Quick technical: what's the input token limit for rerank cross-encoder?
[14:03] Priya: Typical encoder limit is 2048 tokens; for long docs we chunk and score per chunk. We'll include chunking best-practices.
[14:16] Aisha: Do you do prefix caching for frequent queries?
[14:19] Priya: Yes, prefix caching and KV cache for chat contexts; for rerank you can cache candidate embeddings to avoid reembedding.
[14:29] [15:00] Mei: Ok let's talk POC success criteria: improvement in MAP@10 by at least 10% over current baseline, p95 latency < 250ms, and cost under defined threshold.
[15:12] Carlos: Good measurable goals. We'll define instrumentation for those metrics.
[15:20] Aisha: Timeline? We want POC started in two weeks.
[15:24] Carlos: We can aim for kickoff next Tuesday. I'll send a calendar invite.
[15:30] Priya: I'll also provision a temporary higher quota for the team.
[15:34] Liam: Appreciate it.
[15:38] [16:00] Aisha: A quick nit — any limits on candidate payload size? We have long docs (2–3k words).
[16:08] Priya: For long docs we recommend sending truncated passages or chunking; rerank works best on focused passages. There's an attachments API pattern for chunking.
[16:20] Mei: Also curious about cost model for embeddings storage when running locally vs hosted vector db.
[16:25] Carlos: Cost for storage is separate; hosted inference bills per-token or per-request; storage depends on where you host vectors. We'll map this in the benchmark.
[16:40] [18:00] Priya: Wrapping demo up — I'll share the rerank notebook and the Console links. Attaching a short playbook: sample curl, FAISS example, and an eval harness.
[18:16] Aisha: Perfect. Any blockers you foresee?
[18:20] Priya: Only typical ones — dataset formatting, token limits, and procurement paperwork. We can help template the legal docs.
[18:30] Carlos: Ok let's recap actions.
[18:34] [18:40] Carlos: Recap: 1) Priya sends rerank demo code + benchmark sheet; 2) Carlos shares pricing and POC terms; 3) Aisha to share sample dataset and success criteria; 4) schedule POC kickoff next Tuesday.
[18:55] Aisha: Sounds good.
[19:00] Mei: One last question — do you support multi-language embeddings?
[19:05] Priya: Yes — our embed models cover commonly used languages; for rare languages we can evaluate.
[19:12] Liam: Ok thanks team, we'll reconvene after we review the materials.
[19:18] Carlos: Thanks everyone, will follow up with an email and the attachments.
[19:25] [End meeting]
